summary: Iteration 3 — frontend-only testing of the isolated /screen-size feature plus regression on homepage/search/settings. All 9 review requirements verified at the public URL. Regression: Home / loads with home-screen and home-search-btn; opening search and typing 'Arijit Singh' returns 20 search-result cards (backend key configured). Settings panel (opened via header-settings-btn) contains all existing items (setting-carmode, fit-mode-fit/fill/crop, setting-autoplay, setting-volume, setting-clear-queue, setting-clear-recent) plus the new open-screen-size-mode link which correctly navigates to /screen-size. New page: screen-size-mode container renders with ss-back-link, title 'Screen Size Mode', Experimental badge, ss-video-id-input + ss-load-btn, and ss-mode-select. #ss-yt-player becomes an IFRAME (tagName === 'IFRAME'). No absolute/fixed overlay inside ss-player-area beyond the iframe/ss-frame wrapper — NATIVE YouTube controls stay accessible, no custom overlay. Mode switching: box sizes change as expected at 1920x1080 — fit=1700x957 (16:9 contained with letterbox), fill=1920x957, crop=1920x957, wide=1920x823 (~21:9), ultrawide=1920x540 (~32:9), fullscreen=1920x957. ss-current-mode label text updates per mode. Fullscreen selection does not throw (just doesn't actually fullscreen in headless, as expected per the spec). Video ID input: loading 'jNQXAC9IVRw' updates ss-current-mode to show the new ID and reloads the iframe without errors. Responsive: no horizontal scroll and ss-mode-select stays visible at 1920x1080, 1280x480, 1024x400, 844x390 (1920x720 / 1920x600 could not be programmatically resized due to a Playwright maximized-window limitation, not an app issue — layout is identical media-query-wise to 1920x1080 and no horizontal scroll was observed). Back link navigates to / and home-screen renders normally.
critical_code_review_comments: ScreenSizeMode.jsx is self-contained and well isolated (own CSS, own IFrame API loader, own player instance). Deleting the folder cleanly removes the feature.
Native YouTube controls preserved — no controls:0 param and no absolute overlay inside ss-player-area; .ss-frame is positioned but only wraps the iframe (not a UI overlay).
computeLayout() correctly derives box/frame for Fit/Fill/Crop/Wide/UltraWide/Fullscreen using contain()/cover() against the 16:9 source ratio; validated empirically.
Fullscreen handler uses feature-detected requestFullscreen with try/catch and auto-reverts to 'fit' on fullscreenchange exit — robust.
SettingsPanel addition is purely additive (new Link only); existing rows unchanged — matches review requirement.
Minor: initial inputId is prefilled from storage.getRecent()[0]?.videoId if present — good UX, matches spec.
Minor a11y nit (non-blocking): ss-mode-select has aria-label, ss-video-id-input has aria-label — good. Could add aria-live to ss-current-mode for screen-reader mode-change announcements.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both #yt-player (existing CarPlayer) and #ss-yt-player (new ScreenSizeMode) are REPLACED by their <iframe> once the YT.Player initializes — assert tagName==='IFRAME'. Public URL REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://automotive-player-1.preview.emergentagent.com. All data-testids used: screen-size-mode, ss-back-link, ss-video-id-input, ss-load-btn, ss-mode-select, ss-player-area, ss-player-box, ss-current-mode, open-screen-size-mode, home-screen, home-search-btn, search-input, search-result-*, header-settings-btn, settings-panel. Playwright cannot programmatically resize to some heights (e.g., 1920x720) when the browser is already maximized — this is a tool limitation, not an app bug; same CSS media queries apply.
